title: A Completed Instance keeps live Active Data controllers, so payment records stay writable after the relationship ends
content:
The Summer.fi Instance sits in the Distribution Reward Primitive's Completed Instances directory (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.1.3.1), yet its Data Repository is not frozen. Both Active Data controllers remain in force with unchanged terms: "The Responsible Party is Operational GovOps. The Update Process must follow the protocol for 'Direct Edit'" (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.1.3.1.3.1 and .3.2).

So `Completed` closes the *relationship*, not the *record*. Reward periods that ended before completion may still need to be reconciled and paid, and disputes may surface after the fact — a status transition that revoked write access would force the Instance to be reopened, or push the accounting outside the Artifact entirely.

The partner payment address is likewise retained rather than cleared: A.6.1.1.4.2.5.1.3.1.3.2.0.6.2 still records `Summer.fi - 0xC7b548AD9Cf38721810246C079b2d8083aba8909`. The settlement destination outlives the partnership, which is exactly what a trailing payment needs.

There is a pointed contrast here with the live side of the primitive. This concluded Instance has a complete parameter set — Reward Code `1001`, a named Tracking Methodology, a concrete payment address — while three *Active* Instances (ParaSwap, MOM, Lazy Summer Protocol) still defer their payment addresses to a future Artifact iteration. Completeness in this Artifact tracks how long a relationship has existed, not what status it currently holds, so lifecycle status is a poor proxy for how well specified an Instance is.
description: The concluded Summer.fi Instance retains Operational GovOps as Responsible Party under Direct Edit, letting trailing payments and corrections be recorded without reopening the Instance.
